title: Sep 17 Results + Sep 18 Preview: Five Wins on a Solid Pitcher's Night

## Sep 17 Recap: The Strong Arms Delivered

From a pitcher's perspective, yesterday was all about trusting the arms we backed. When you go 5-4 on a nine-game slate, you're staying above water and banking profit. The misses? Two coin-flip games at 50-51% that could've gone either way, plus a couple tough breaks. But our confident picks—the ones in the 61-63% range—went 5-for-5. That's what I like to see.

content.title: Sep 17 Prediction Results by Confidence Level

content.value:
## What Worked Yesterday

The Astros, Rays, and Padres picks were textbook. When you've got the pitching edge and the home field or better lineup, you ride that wave. The Angels and White Sox plays were grittier, but they came through when it mattered.

The four misses were all essentially toss-ups. The Brewers-Pirates game at 52%? That's margin-of-error stuff. Same with the two 50% picks on the Reds and Mets—those are games where one hanging slider changes everything. The Tigers miss at 51% stung a bit, but that's baseball. You tip your cap and move on.

## Sep 18 Preview: Reds Over Cubs

Tomorrow's top play takes us right back to Cincinnati, and this time I'm more confident. The Cubs are sending Clay Holmes to the bump—a guy who's been converted from a reliever role and is still finding his footing as a starter. Opposing him is Chase Burns for the Reds, a young arm with electric stuff who's been locating well at home.

From a pitcher's perspective, this matchup favors the Reds. Holmes has bullpen DNA—short bursts, max effort. Stretching him out past the fifth inning is where things get dicey. Burns, meanwhile, has shown he can work deeper into games with better command of his secondary pitches. Add in the Reds' home field advantage at Great American Ball Park, and you've got a recipe for a Cincinnati win.

## The Pitching Matchup Breakdown

**Clay Holmes (Cubs):** Transitioned from high-leverage relief to starting rotation. His sinker-slider combo plays well in short stints, but third-time-through-the-order exposure has been his Achilles heel. Expect the Cubs to lean heavily on their bullpen.

**Chase Burns (Reds):** The young righty has been impressive at home, generating weak contact and missing bats with a plus changeup. His ability to work 6+ innings gives the Reds' bullpen a breather and keeps their defense engaged.

This isn't a blowout call at 50%, but it's a smart play based on pitching dynamics. Trust the arm that's built for the starter's workload.

## Final Thought

Yesterday we proved that when we lean into our high-confidence picks, we cash tickets. Today's Reds play might be lower confidence on paper, but the pitching matchup tells me everything I need to know. Ride with Burns at home, and let's keep the momentum rolling into the weekend.

**- Ace**
